filename: Evaluating the effects of precipitation and evapotranspiration on soil moisture variability.pdf
title: Evaluating the effects of precipitation and evapotranspiration on soil moisture variability
code_availability: The codes and data for analysis in this study are available at https://purr.purdue.edu/publications/3999/1.
testbed_rationale: This paper performs diagnostic spectral analysis and model intercomparison using linear time-invariant transfer functions and Fourier transforms, rather than providing or benchmarking machine learning parameterizations or emulators.
pain_points: Temporal discontinuity in daily satellite observations requires gap-filling before spectral Fourier analysis.
Spatial resolution mismatch between coarse CMIP5 ESM grids and 36 km observational grids requires re-gridding.
Observational uncertainties and retrieval errors in SMAP over densely vegetated, frozen, or water-body-adjacent terrain.
Non-linearities and time-variant processes (vegetation canopy interception, snow accumulation/melting, runoff) challenge the linear time-invariant (LTI) assumption of land hydrology.
extraction_notes: The study does not develop or evaluate machine learning models; it applies classical signal processing (Fast Fourier Transform, LTI transfer functions, spectral slope/noise coloring) to diagnose CMIP5 land surface performance.
